mechanism_narrative: A downward trend in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS shows a downward trend over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a labor market slowdown that triggers a shift in investor sentiment toward defensive equities, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.2%), the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.2%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 100 (the 2017 base level), it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months indicates strong labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS shows an upward trend over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) signals economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when quarterly GDP growth is positive, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 1.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates for equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
